title: How to well-design semantical interaction - which users actually care??
original:
Semantical yet Smooth Interaction
Most of the existing interactions: are non-semantical (Bodily movement, Rafael Lozano Hemmer, Just simple scrolling)
Why?
Semantical interaction (i.e. interaction where the user provides meaning/interacts within context) makes it hard to expect active user engagement within an exhibition context
User 쭈뼛쭈뼛 혹은 비협조적/Dummy Text Input
Ex. Chunk of Text Input, Voice Interaction

Possible workaround:
Make user's non-active/passive interaction itself as part of the semantical interaction itself (Non-active/passive interaction itself is an interaction) 
As technology advances, Face Tracking is a strong example of such interaction
On-boarding 1: Strong Intro (V-Effekt): Immediately grabs user's attention & 
On-boarding 2: Gradual Intro: Make the user relax, Smooth Incremental Engagement
On-boarding 3: Strong Background Storytelling/Pre-given context
Dadaism or Interaction-Dimensional Transformation: Input A, Output AAAAAAAA some kind of dadaistic exaggeration or fun/unexpected input-output relationship (dimensional transformation)
Can be for example transforming non-semantical interaction (low information input) into very highly semantical output (Amplifying/Exaggerating information)
Can be used for VUI-based interaction: Simple voice input, Passive murmuring → Gives a hell lot of context and transforms into strong/affirmative output
Queuing experience: Have a long queue outside (People will interact harder as they want to compensate for their queuing - and know that thereis a  value in the interaction)

In this case: Making non-active/passive interaction as the part of the interaction, as well as amplifying the user's voice input interaction (Normally LLM-VUI situation: user leads the context, but in this case, LLM leads the context!), as well as giving strong intro - user doesn’t know there will be interaction when they are trying to take some rest, but apparently, the interaction starts unexpectedly as user lies down on the bed!
english:
How can a semantic interaction ask something meaningful of a participant without making them reluctant to engage?

Many exhibition interactions depend on bodily movement or a simple gesture. Asking someone to compose text or speak within a specific context is harder. They may hesitate, refuse, or enter something arbitrary. The work cannot assume that every visitor arrives ready to contribute an articulate response.

One approach is to make that hesitation part of the interaction. Inactivity, a face or a small involuntary response can carry the exchange forward. Another is to reconsider the introduction: an immediate estranging event, a gradual invitation that lets someone settle in, or a strong narrative context established before their first action.

A third approach transforms the scale of the input. A small, low-information action can produce an unexpectedly rich semantic response. Input A becomes output AAAAAAAA. That disproportion can be funny, Dadaist or disorienting. A murmur, for instance, could cause a voice interface to respond with extravagant conviction.

In a conventional language-model interface, the user supplies the context and leads the conversation. Here the model could lead, treating a minimal or passive response as enough to continue. I also noted the way a queue may raise a visitor’s expectations and investment, although waiting is not itself the artistic experience.

The particular scenario I am considering begins with rest. Someone lies down on a bed without expecting an interaction. The system addresses them, and their uncertain response becomes part of the exchange. The introduction, the amplification of a small vocal input and the inclusion of passivity all belong to the same design problem.
